market_question: Will Dan Cox win the 2026 Maryland Governor Republican primary election?
reasoning: Dan Cox has no official campaign, is still over a year from the primary, and carries the baggage of a 30-point general-election loss in 2022. The field is likely to include other high-profile contenders like Representative Andy Harris, and party insiders are signaling a desire for a more electable candidate. Assigning a 57.5% probability to a single non-incumbent this early is excessive; a more realistic range is 40–45%.
evidence_points: Cox lost the 2022 general election by 32 points, raising electability concerns within the party.
Reports from The Baltimore Sun and Washington Post in early 2025 indicate serious interest from other Republicans, including Congressman Andy Harris, who would split the conservative base.
Open gubernatorial primaries far from the election rarely see a single candidate above 50% probability absent commanding polls, which are absent here.
sources_consulted: Baltimore Sun – 2025 Maryland Republican gubernatorial primary speculation
Washington Post – January 2025 article on potential Maryland GOP candidates
Historical primary forecast literature – early-stage candidate probabilities
